title: The Worst Cause Of Teacher Stress
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies what he considers the single most exhausting and avoidable source of teacher stress: relying on words, persuasion, and personal charisma to convince students to behave, rather than letting a classroom management plan do the work. He describes the toll of this approach — lectures, pep-talks, threats, false praise — as both stressful for the teacher and ultimately counterproductive, since it worsens misbehavior over time. He states plainly that he could not sustain a teaching career built on this model of constant persuasion. His solution is a clear reallocation of responsibility: teachers should teach great lessons and protect students' right to learn, while students bear responsibility for listening, learning, and behaving according to class rules. Practically, this means teachers must stop trying to talk students into compliance and instead let natural consequences, delivered through a consistent plan, do the heavy lifting — a shift he promises will lighten both stress and improve behavior.
points: Trying to talk, persuade, or cajole students into good behavior is the most stressful and ultimately counterproductive approach to classroom management.
This approach mistakenly puts responsibility for student behavior onto the teacher rather than the student.
A clear division of responsibility — teacher teaches and protects, student listens and behaves — restores balance and reduces stress.
Teachers should stop persuading, dealmaking, and flattering, and instead let a classroom management plan do the work.
Shifting responsibility appropriately to students improves their maturity, motivation, and classroom behavior over time.
quotes: The worst cause of teacher stress is trying to convince students to behave. It’s a reliance on your words to get them under control.
This approach to managing students manifests itself in the form of lectures, talking-tos, pep-talks, and threats. Intimidation and false praise are also telltale signs.
If relying on my wits and words were my primary way of curbing misbehavior, I’d find another profession. To smile through such burden day after day is agony.

The teacher’s responsibility is to teach great lessons, protect the rights of every student to learn and enjoy school, and create an environment they all look forward to. The student’s responsibility is to listen, learn, and behave according to the rules of the class.
Instead, follow the laws of the real world and let them experience the full weight of your consequences, all on their own and without cushioning their fall.
A grand piano will slide off your shoulders. Your smile will be real. And your students will thrive.
